en: The Jātaka:
The Section of Eleven, Chapter on the Supporter of His Mother.
2. The Juṇha Jātaka:
“Listen to my words, O Lord of Men;
I have come here for a purpose, Juṇha.”
“O Best of the Lords of Bipeds, they say one should not pass by while a traveling Brahmin stands waiting.
“I am listening; I shall stop. Speak, O Brahmā.”
"For what purpose have you arrived here?
What goal do you seek from me, O Brahmā, that you have come? Please tell me that."
“Give me five choice villages,
seven hundred female slaves, and seven hundred oxen,
and more than a thousand gold coins.”
"Give me two wives who are my equals.
Is it your asceticism, O Brahmin, that has such a form?
Or is it your wisdom, O Brahmin, that has such a form?"
Do you have any yakṣas who are obedient to you?
Or do you know how to accomplish my purpose?
I possess neither ascetic power nor spells.
I have no yakkhas whatsoever who are obedient to me;
nor do I recognize any task for you to perform,
though there was previously a mere meeting with you.
"This is the first time I have known this vision;
I do not recognize anything prior to this.
Being asked, tell me the meaning of this."
When or where was our meeting? O Lord,
we lived in the delightful city of the King of Gandhāra and in Takkasilā.
There, in the darkness among the timisika fish,
we pressed shoulder to shoulder.
Standing there together, O Lord of Men, we both—
There we exchanged friendly greetings; that alone was our meeting,
and after that, there was neither before nor after.
Whenever, O Brahmā,
a meeting with a true person occurs among human beings,
the wise do not [cling] to associations or intimacy.
They destroy even what was done in the past.
Indeed, fools, through their associations and intimacy,
destroy even what was done in the past.
Even much that is done for fools goes to waste,
for fools are by nature ungrateful;
but the wise indeed value association and intimacy.
They do not let even what was done in the past go to waste;
among the wise, even a small good deed does not perish,
for the wise are those who recognize well-done deeds.
I give you five excellent cows,
seven hundred female slaves, and eight hundred oxen,
as well as more than a thousand gold coins.
"And I shall give you two wives equal to yourself.
Thus it is for the virtuous when they meet together, O King,
like the king of constellations among the stars."
“Just as the *kāśī* cloth is filled [with scent],
so too have I obtained union with you today.
The Second Juṇha Jātaka.
